claims: n90/n90_exact.json states 90 unit squares as [center_x, center_y, cos, sin] rows of exact rationals, (cos, sin) the unit direction of one edge, with the side 99940387666098521323/10000000000000000000; #997 and the root README round it up at 12 places as 9.994038766610, and n90/README.md prints 9.9940387666098521323. n90/n90_witness.yaml states the same packing as a packing.squares:Witness/v2 document of rational corners with the softschema envelope and a claim block of coordinate_provenance reported. #997 says the side is 9e-8 below that of #996's certificate (64d5ee7), which it replaces, and asks that fa53fb0 be pinned and the earlier commit disregarded; n90/README.md compares the side with the record's 9.998277166926 at 90 (T-303), an improvement of 0.00424.

n90/README.md and n90/REGISTRATION.md say the packing starts from T-303, which jazivxt built from a crop of the source's n = 157 packing: T-303 has a cluster of 44 squares that lean away from the axes inside a frame of axis-aligned squares; a local search changed small groups of squares in position and angle, optimized the packing again after each change and kept the changes that gave a smaller side; in the new packing the cluster has 40 leaning squares, four squares in the upper left of the cluster are axis-aligned, four squares at the top of the cluster lean by 25.1 and 27.8 degrees where T-303 has 22.9 degrees, and one axis-aligned square at the top wall lies 0.32 lower. They say a linear program over all 90 squares, with every contact linearized at the solution, found no first-order improvement larger than 4e-10, that an earlier packing of this arrangement passed the same test at a side 9e-8 larger, so the test covers one set of contacts, that the certificate keeps a smallest gap of 2e-12 between squares, and that the local optimum has no formal proof. They say a public merged Kaggle submission (bestbryant/claude_code_squaresinsquares, 15 November 2026) lists 9.998277166917 for n = 90 and that the leaderboard's best sides were not available.

verify_exact.py (separating axes) and check_area.py (the area of each close pair's clipped intersection), both Python's fractions.Fraction and its standard library only, are the folder's two exact checkers; #997 says each reports 90 squares and 199 close pairs on the new files, that this repository's check_rational_witness_independent.py reports 'VERIFIED: 90 squares, 4005 pairs' on the witness, and that the witness validates against this repository's witness.schema.yaml with 0 errors. #996 says the two checkers have one author and read the same input file but share no code. #997 says the arrangement, lineage, credit and AI assistance are as #996 states: credit to Joost de Winter as an improvement of jazivxt's packing; the local search run with GPT-6.1 Sol Max (OpenAI) and the local optimization, rational certificate, checks and figures produced with Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), both under his direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
